text:
Situation: Sodium acetate has been on FDA's shortage list since 2016-02-03 and remains current as of 2026-10-21. Corvale East holds four lots totaling 748 vials (5.6–35.9 days). Corvale General holds four lots totaling 1,026 vials (14.3–29.4 days). Combined supply covers roughly 10–30 days depending on site.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the shortage on 2016-02-03; status is still current as of 2026-10-21. Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1021343) received OAI classifications after inspections ending 2010-01-19, 2011-06-17, and 2011-08-04, all before the shortage posting. Pfizer Healthcare India Private Limited (FEI 3008316085) received an OAI classification after an inspection ending 2019-09-06, with the classification letter dated 2020-05-25. Both plants also have multiple VAI inspections before and after the shortage posting.

Our position: Current inventory is limited and variable across sites. The rule-based best option is Amneal Pharmaceuticals Private Limited, which is not on FDA's shortage list today, but its label names no plant we could place. Other suppliers (B. Braun, Baxter, ICU Medical) also lack identifiable plants on their labels. Hikma's sodium acetate 164 mg/mL is FDA-listed as Current (posted 2016-02-03) and was approved by Sam Rivera, MD on 2026-08-19 for alternate concentration or vial size, pending pharmacist verification.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to identify and qualify Amneal's manufacturing site; if qualified, initiate purchase. Approval: P&T Committee.
2. Buyer to identify and qualify manufacturing sites for B. Braun, Baxter, and ICU Medical as backup sources. Approval: P&T Committee.
3. Pharmacist to verify dosing and volume for Hikma's sodium acetate 164 mg/mL if selected. Approval: Pharmacy Director.

Not recommended: Switching to any alternate product without confirmed site qualification and pharmacist verification.
